findings.name: three.js (r186 / npm 0.186.1)
findings.what_it_does: Core WebGL/WebGPU 3D engine. r186 adds SunLight (WebGPU), TSL SSAO/GTAO/OIT nodes and Gaussian splats; WebGPURenderer can force a WebGL2 backend (read in source). Hub for R3F, That Open and the Rhino 3dm loader.
findings.how_we_use_it: Pin 0.186.x with WebGLRenderer behind one renderer adapter; stock materials where possible. Use built-in loaders (OBJ, glTF, 3DM), GLTFExporter, clipping planes. Fit camera near/far per frame; test reversedDepthBuffer in a spike. WebGPURenderer and TSL spike after 10 Dec.
findings.saves: Biggest ecosystem; Claude knows its API well (expected, not measured), so fewer tokens on docs and fixes.
findings.risks: Releases deprecate APIs (r186 removed PCFSoftShadowMap); WebGPU path maturing; float32 needs a local origin; reversedDepthBuffer is init-time, needs EXT_clip_control (Firefox about 2% per third-party stats) and excludes logarithmic depth.

findings.name: react-three-fiber (R3F) v9.8.2
findings.what_it_does: React renderer for three.js; v9 targets React 19. v10 alpha (alpha.6, 2026-10-17) makes WebGPU default. In 9.8.2, shadows={true} sets PCFSoftShadowMap, which r186 replaces with PCFShadowMap plus a console warning (read in source).
findings.how_we_use_it: Pin R3F 9.8.x with react 19.3.x. frameloop=demand, shadows=percentage (explicit PCFShadowMap). Use performance.regress with drei AdaptiveDpr during interaction; calibrate the quality tier once at startup. Cache node thumbnails as images, not live Views. Skip v10 alpha for 13 Nov.
findings.saves: Declarative scene code is shorter for Claude to write and review; drei supplies most helpers.
findings.risks: Peer range react >=19 <19.4 limits upgrades; shadows=true or soft triggers the removed PCFSoft mode; v10 changes renderer defaults and GLSL libraries need a legacy path; some add-ons stale (@react-three/a11y, 2022).

findings.name: @react-three/drei 10.7.9
findings.what_it_does: Helper library for R3F: Edges (EdgesGeometry, one Line2 per mesh), Outlines (inverted hull), Line, CameraControls, PerformanceMonitor, AdaptiveDpr, Bvh, Html, Grid, Sky, AccumulativeShadows, SoftShadows, View (multi-viewport in one Canvas).
findings.how_we_use_it: Main viewport toolbox. Edges only for small imported objects; massing and context use worker-computed line segments. Outlines for hover, CameraControls for bookmarks, AdaptiveDpr for interaction-time DPR, Html for labels. PerformanceMonitor only for startup calibration or tours. No View thumbnails.
findings.saves: Replaces weeks of custom helpers; documented components keep prompts short.
findings.risks: PerformanceMonitor samples only rendered frames, so idle gaps under frameloop=demand read as low fps (source read); Edges runs on the main thread per mesh; View calls gl.render directly, bypassing EffectComposer; SoftShadows untested on r186.

findings.name: pmndrs/postprocessing 6.39.5 + @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1
findings.what_it_does: WebGL post-processing: Outline, SSAO, SMAA, tone mapping, depth. @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 depends on n8ao ^2.0.0 and exports an N8AO pass, plus Kuwahara, Halftone, Linocut and Ramp for diagrammatic looks.
findings.how_we_use_it: Inside EffectComposer: N8AO (halfRes), SMAA, tone mapping, selection Outline. Set multisampling={0}: wrapper default is 4 and N8AO says hardware antialiasing fails with AO. Halftone and Kuwahara only in board-diagram presets. No custom N8AO wrapper.
findings.saves: Ready-made effects, including AO, instead of hand-written shaders or wrappers.
findings.risks: Peer three <0.187 blocks upgrades; v7 still beta; GLSL passes legacy under WebGPU; HalfFloat default buffers raise capture memory; Outline's mask pass uses an override material, which skips per-material clipping planes (source read, not run).

findings.name: N8AO 2.0.1
findings.what_it_does: Ambient-occlusion pass for three.js with quality presets, optional neural denoise, halfRes (README claims 2x-4x speedup), accumulation for still cameras. Ships as <N8AO /> inside @react-three/postprocessing. Renders the scene itself; aoRadius is in world units by default.
findings.how_we_use_it: Default AO for the clay look: <N8AO halfRes depthAwareUpsampling /> with world-space aoRadius. Accumulate when the camera rests (call invalidate() under a demand loop). Set quality once at startup (changes recompile shaders). Lock n8ao 2.0.1 in the lockfile; the wrapper allows ^2.0.0. Off in the Low tier.
findings.saves: Strong depth cues for the cost of one pass, no custom AO or wrapper code.
findings.risks: WebGL only; hardware MSAA does not work with AO, use SMAA; README and GitHub say CC0-1.0 but npm lists ISC; one maintainer, 503 stars; speedup figures are vendor claims; README documents no fixed noise seed for tiled captures.
findings.license: CC0-1.0 per README and GitHub (npm: ISC)

findings.name: three-mesh-bvh 0.9.16
findings.what_it_does: Bounding-volume hierarchy for fast raycasts and spatial queries on three.js meshes; async/worker builds, BatchedMesh support, GPU SDF and path-tracing examples. Foundation for three-edge-projection and three-bvh-csg.
findings.how_we_use_it: Fast picking on large context meshes and imported BIM, built only over the analysis domain. Cast rays from grid points toward the sun for solar-access and shadow-hour modules without a GPU readback.
findings.saves: Avoids writing spatial indexing; one dependency covers picking and analysis.
findings.risks: README performance claim (500 rays on 80k polygons at 60 fps) is untested on student laptops; BVH build time and memory on huge context or IFC models; essentially one maintainer; 86 open issues+PRs.

findings.name: Manifold (manifold-3d 3.5.4)
findings.what_it_does: Guaranteed-manifold mesh boolean library in WASM. d.ts confirms twist/scale extrude, slice(height) on the X-Y plane (Z-up), volume, project, splitByPlane, hull, offset, originalID/faceID tracking and an ExecutionContext (cancel, progress).
findings.how_we_use_it: Worker massing kernel in Z-up metres: floorplate stacks, podium and tower unions, site cuts, per-floor gross area via slice() at mid-storey, sections via splitByPlane. reserveIDs per program volume so tags survive booleans (add test). Progress and cancel via withContext plus status().
findings.saves: One robust kernel for massing, areas, sections and tag tracking; avoids heavy B-rep WASM (about 2.8 MB unpacked package).
findings.risks: Triangle meshes only; JS Mesh is Float32, so local coordinates; inputs must be manifold; 3.5.4 declares esbuild-wasm and gltf-transform as non-optional peers plus runtime dependencies (install footprint, bundle size unchecked); manual delete(); STL export discouraged.
findings.popularity: 2.4k stars, 272 forks; used by OpenSCAD, Blender, Godot, Babylon.js per README

findings.name: rhino3dm.js 8.35.0 + three Rhino3dmLoader
findings.what_it_does: openNURBS compiled to WASM: read/write .3dm, geometry containers, Rhino Compute client. three.js Rhino3dmLoader decodes in workers, meshes SubD, converts Breps from stored per-face meshes and exposes layers, views, groups and file settings in userData.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import .3dm via Rhino3dmLoader with wasm hosted locally (setLibraryPath; docs example uses a CDN). Read userData.settings (modelUnitSystem, modelBasePoint, earthAnchorPoint per typings) to normalise units and position; the loader does not rotate Z-up. Map layers to program tags.
findings.saves: Direct Rhino import with no server; avoids a custom parser.
findings.risks: No booleans or meshing in JS (advanced ops need Rhino Compute); Breps without stored face meshes are skipped with a warning (source read, not run); loader pins 8.32.1 while npm is 8.35.0; unit and anchor fields not yet tested on team files.

findings.name: web-ifc 0.0.78
findings.what_it_does: C++ IFC reader/writer compiled to WASM, multithreaded build. Typings define IFC2X3, IFC4 and IFC4X3 schemas, GetModelSchema, GetCoordinationMatrix, COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN and a linear scaling factor; low-level writer (CreateModel, WriteLine, SaveModel). Same engine under That Open.
findings.how_we_use_it: Import IFC in a worker for 13 Nov with COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN off; read the coordination matrix and IfcMapConversion, apply the unit scaling, place every model against the project site origin in float64. IFC write-back moves to v1 (spike vs ifc-lite, IfcOpenShell). For 13 Nov export glTF and .3dm.
findings.saves: Replaces a custom IFC parser; same engine that That Open and many viewers use.
findings.risks: MPL-2.0 (file-level copyleft); pre-1.0; writer is entity-level (project, storeys, psets built by hand); no unit-query API in typings; Revit IFC MapConversion scale issue reported; schema typings read, not run; 79 open issues+PRs.

findings.name: ifc-lite (LTplus-AG/ifc-lite; @ifc-lite/wasm 10.4.0, parser 9.5.1, export 4.11.0)
findings.what_it_does: Rust/WASM IFC toolkit: parse, query, edit, validate, export (STEP, glTF, Parquet, IFC5). Claims IFC2X3, IFC4, IFC4X3 and IFC5 coverage, exact-arithmetic CSG for openings and a three.js template. Self-reported up to 5x faster than web-ifc.
findings.how_we_use_it: Benchmark beside web-ifc on one real Revit IFC (load time, fidelity, IFC4X3, storey and space export) before choosing the v1 importer. Check @ifc-lite/create for authoring storeys and spaces. Use only behind an importer interface.
findings.saves: Could answer schema coverage and IFC write-back questions that web-ifc leaves open, saving custom writer work.
findings.risks: Young (created 2026-01-10), company-run, MPL-2.0; README STEP export examples show property edits only; speed claims unverified; @ifc-lite/wasm unpacks to 10.5 MB; 432 stars; 41 open issues+PRs.
findings.popularity: 432 stars, 111 forks; one Show HN with 2 points and 0 comments

findings.name: That Open Engine: @thatopen/components 3.4.9 + fragments 3.4.8
findings.what_it_does: MIT toolkit for BIM apps on three.js. worlds.create wires its own SimpleScene, SimpleRenderer and SimpleCamera to a container div. Fragments (3.4.8) loads via model.object and useCamera. Docs show no R3F or existing-renderer path.
findings.how_we_use_it: Spike first: load fragments plus web-ifc straight into the R3F scene and build our own clipper and plan tools, or isolate That Open in a lazy-loaded BIM inspector route. Record the decision. Never run two renderers, cameras and pickers on one page.
findings.saves: Section/plan/measure tooling and a compact binary BIM format for imported models, if the spike succeeds.
findings.risks: Fast-moving 3.x; component list and custom-renderer support not confirmed from docs; performance claims untested; extra bundle weight; two-renderer conflicts if mixed; Fragments README says nothing on IFC export.
findings.last_activity: components pushed 2026-10-19, npm 3.4.9 on 2026-10-06; fragments pushed 2026-10-19

findings.name: xeokit-sdk 2.6.114
findings.what_it_does: Pure-WebGL 3D BIM/IFC viewer SDK with double precision and an XKT pre-converted format; plugins for glTF, CityJSON, LAS. Not built on three.js. Commercial licence sold by Creoox.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not embed. Study its XKT and double-precision ideas only (our local-origin rule covers precision). Revisit only if the platform itself is released under AGPL-3.0.

findings.name: replicad + replicad-opencascadejs 1.1.0
findings.what_it_does: Code-CAD library for the browser on an OpenCascade WASM build. Typings confirm fuse, cut, intersect, fillet, extrude with twistAngle, exportSTEP, blobSTEP and blobSTL; web workbench at studio.replicad.xyz.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 detail module for B-rep parts (facade brackets, connection details) and STEP export, in a worker, loaded on demand. Not used for tower massing, where Manifold is lighter.

findings.risks: One maintainer, 706 stars, 49 open issues+PRs; each replicad-opencascadejs WASM build is about 23 MB (48.8 MB package), LGPL-2.1; docs pages opened gave no worker setup; manual memory care.

findings.name: CadQuery, build123d and OCP.wasm (Python B-rep)
findings.what_it_does: build123d and CadQuery are Python B-rep libraries on OCP/OpenCASCADE with STEP export. Neither is in the official Pyodide package list. Third-party yeicor/OCP.wasm (MIT, 49 stars) runs build123d in Pyodide in the browser; CadQuery in-browser not confirmed.
findings.how_we_use_it: Roadmap only: optional in-browser STEP detail module via OCP.wasm, or a local Python worker. Never core; prefer Manifold or replicad. Prototype after 10 Dec behind a flag, measuring download size and load time first.
findings.saves: None for core; keeps a code-CAD route open without native installs if OCP.wasm proves usable.
findings.risks: OCP.wasm: young (created 2025-05-31), owner yeicor with no listed contributors, download size unstated, full tests Chrome-only, support may vary by browser. Native OCP wheels can be blocked by Windows Smart App Control; CadQuery pip supports Python 3.9-3.12 only.

findings.name: earthtojake/text-to-cad (and Zoo Text-to-CAD, not adopted)
findings.what_it_does: earthtojake/text-to-cad: plugin with 12 agent skills and a local MCP server (cadgen) on build123d; outputs STEP/STL/3MF/GLB. Zoo (KittyCAD modeling-app, MIT) streams its 3D view from a hosted engine; its Text-to-CAD is a credit-based hosted service.
findings.how_we_use_it: Dev-time Claude Code plugin for small mechanical details (brackets, connectors); copy its packaging pattern (skills, local MCP, viewer) for our module-authoring skill. Not for tower massing. Zoo: not core; optional flagged API later, never required offline.
findings.saves: Ready CAD skills; its packaging pattern saves designing our own agent interface.
findings.risks: text-to-cad: no architecture-scale examples; telemetry on by default (opt out); Smart App Control blocks OCP on Windows 11; needs uv, Python 3.11+, Node 20+. Zoo: hosted engine and usage cost, no published benchmarks, KCL licence and local execution unconfirmed.

findings.name: LLM-to-CAD research: Text-to-CadQuery, CADCodeVerify, cad0, Text2BIM
findings.what_it_does: Single-part results: Text-to-CadQuery best top-1 exact match 69.3%; CADCodeVerify visual self-check +5.0% (GPT-4); cad0 weak out-of-distribution. Text2BIM (arXiv 2408.08054) adds an LLM agent loop with a rule-based checker for building models, no metrics given.
findings.how_we_use_it: Constrained text-to-massing: the LLM returns a flat JSON node list (enum types, id references, params as name/value pairs) via structured outputs (Claude output_config json_schema, OpenAI strict); Manifold validates; we render and check; human edits. Copy Text2BIM's checker-and-repair loop. No free-form CAD in core.
findings.saves: Prevents spending build time on unreliable free-form text-to-CAD; schema-constrained JSON is cheap in tokens and needs fewer retries.
findings.risks: Evidence is single parts or one prototype, not towers; paper numbers not reproduced; Claude schemas reject recursion and numeric/array bounds (400 error) while OpenAI allows them, so our validator owns bounds; HN thread (about 10 voices) says LLMs are weak at spatial reasoning.
findings.maintainer: Xie and Ju (Text-to-CadQuery); Alrashedy et al. (CADCodeVerify); campedersen (cad0); Du, Esser, Nousias, Borrmann (Text2BIM)
findings.last_activity: Papers: May 2025, Oct 2024 (rev. Feb 2025); Text2BIM Aug 2024 (rev. Jul 2025)

findings.name: JSCAD (@jscad/modeling 2.13.0)
findings.what_it_does: MIT modular JavaScript CAD for browser and CLI. @jscad/modeling offers BSP-tree CSG booleans, extrusions, hulls, expansions and measurements; online editor at openjscad.xyz. Marked stable, user-group maintained.
findings.how_we_use_it: Do not adopt for massing; Manifold gives guaranteed-manifold output and far faster booleans. Keep JSCAD only as inspiration for a code-CAD node, and reuse the Manifold JS API for that node instead.
findings.saves: Avoids a second CSG kernel and its manifoldness checks.
findings.risks: BSP booleans: one anecdotal test shows 35 s vs 0.07 s against Manifold and a non-manifold result; README gives no robustness or worker guidance; slice and area support unconfirmed; 159 open issues+PRs.

findings.name: Hairline (lucasmarkes/hairline, npm @lucasmarkes/hairline 0.5.1)
findings.what_it_does: 33 pointer-responsive isometric line figures as SVG with a React entry. Six theme tokens (plate, hi, edge, mid, lo, stroke width), one shared animation loop that sleeps when idle, springs on some figures, reduced-motion support, hairline-create and hairline-adopt skills.
findings.how_we_use_it: Use tokens for UI illustrations, module-card thumbnails, empty states and onboarding. Apply the plate/edge/mid/lo ladder to viewport colours. Take interaction rules from Anatomy motion.md or mark them team assumptions. Generate custom figures with hairline-create sparingly.
findings.saves: Ready-made calm visual language; skills avoid hand-drawing icons.
findings.risks: README states no hit-area, easing, rest-pose or single-accent rule; needs a DOM (no SSR); plate colour set by hand on non-default backgrounds; About text says six figures vs README 33.

findings.name: Anatomy (wheresryan22/anatomy)
findings.what_it_does: MIT agent skill that turns a concept into an interactive isometric machine in shaded SVG, optional WebGL shaders and a beta 3D mode. References (motion, 3d, webgl, craft) were read; the documented example took about 1 h 54 min of agent time.
findings.how_we_use_it: One or two hero explainers only. Borrow motion.md rules (spring-like following, loop sleeps when idle, reduced motion jumps to end state, one lit accent) and webgl.md rules (DPR cap 1.5, stop idle loops); adopt its geometry audit idea.
findings.saves: Hero illustrations without a designer, at a high one-off cost; its reference files give citable motion and WebGL rules.
findings.risks: Slow and token-heavy by design; non-deterministic outputs; 3D mode beta; created 2026-10-08, very young; abstract ideas give labelled boxes; 61 open issues+PRs.

findings.name: three-edge-projection (GitHub-only, v0.0.10)
findings.what_it_does: Projects visible and hidden mesh edges along the Y axis into 2D line segments; PlanarIntersectionGenerator slices with a plane; SilhouetteGenerator uses clipper2-js. package.json exports worker and webgpu entries. Built on three-mesh-bvh.
findings.how_we_use_it: v1 hidden-line plan and roof views, plus axon views by pre-rotating the scene (our inference, untested) with dashed hidden edges. Section lines via PlanarIntersectionGenerator or Manifold slice. Install from a pinned commit (3ac00e1, 2026-09-30); write SVG with our own exporter.
findings.saves: Hidden-line projection and plane sections without writing a rasteriser or section code.
findings.risks: Not on npm (0.0.3 published then unpublished 2025-10-28): install from GitHub. Stale peers (three ^0.155, three-mesh-bvh ^0.6.0) clash with ours, so use overrides. Axon pre-rotation untested; worker entry undocumented in README.

findings.name: three.js CSM addon, SunLight and takram atmosphere (later)
findings.what_it_does: CSM (cascaded shadow maps, WebGLRenderer only; 3 cascades, 2048 maps by default) patches materials via onBeforeCompile (setupMaterial). SunLight is documented for WebGPU. takram three-atmosphere (beta) is a later photoreal sky; its API is being rewritten.
findings.how_we_use_it: One-day spike on 0.186.1: a single directional light with its shadow camera fitted to the analysis domain (4096 map) vs CSM through one material factory calling csm.setupMaterial. Use CSM only if near-camera shadows look poor; drop SoftShadows from core. drei Sky now, takram later.
findings.saves: Built-in large-scene shadows if CSM is needed; takram would later avoid custom atmosphere shaders.
findings.risks: CSM and drei SoftShadows patch shaders and will not port to WebGPU; PCFSoftShadowMap removed in r186; combination untested here; heavy on integrated GPUs (Low tier: one map); SunLight WebGL support unconfirmed; takram has beta and alpha parts.

findings.name: SunCalc (mourner/suncalc) 2.1.1
findings.what_it_does: Dependency-free JS for sun position (getPosition returns altitude and azimuth in degrees, azimuth clockwise from north) and sun times with a utcOffset option. v2 is a precision-focused rewrite with breaking changes; README cites Meeus, USNO and JPL Horizons validation.
findings.how_we_use_it: Pin 2.1.1 and drive viewport sun and the sun/shadow module for Vancouver (49.28 N) through one wrapper. Unit-test against published reference values (JPL Horizons or USNO; NOAA page says it is no longer maintained). Use IANA America/Vancouver. Note v2 conventions in CLAUDE.md.
findings.saves: Tiny, well known; no astronomy code to write.
findings.risks: v2 conventions differ from v1 tutorials and model memory (south-based radians), so generated code can be silently wrong; npm licence field blank (GitHub shows BSD-2-Clause); time zone and DST handling is ours.
findings.license: BSD-2-Clause per GitHub (npm field blank; README states none)

findings.name: Section and explode references: three.js clipping + stencil caps; three-cad-viewer 5.1.3

If Outline leaks, use renderer-level clippingPlanes. Borrow explode and tree patterns from three-cad-viewer; do not embed.
findings.saves: Proven section recipe and a working explode-plus-AO-plus-edges example for Claude to copy.
findings.risks: Needs closed meshes; one cap pass per plane; WebGL-specific; Outline's override-material mask pass skips per-material clipping (source read); stencil plus composer plus N8AO untested; three-cad-viewer uses a custom shapes format, one maintainer.

findings.name: 3DTilesRendererJS (3d-tiles-renderer 0.5.3)

findings.name: Node.js 24 LTS (24.22.x) + Vite 8.3.5 toolchain
findings.what_it_does: Node schedule: v24 entered Maintenance 2026-10-20 (supported to 2028-04-30); v22 Maintenance since 2025-10-21 (ends 2027-04-30); v26 becomes LTS 2026-10-28. Vite 8.3.5 (published 2026-10-21) needs Node ^20.19 or >=22.12.
findings.how_we_use_it: Install Node 24.22.x now (24.22.1 released 2026-10-20); pin in .nvmrc and package.json engines; do not start on 22. Node 26 optional after 28 Oct. Use npm with a committed lockfile and npm ci; check the Vite bundle report.
findings.saves: One install decision that avoids a mid-project runtime change and mismatched student machines.
findings.risks: Node 24 is Maintenance (fixes only) but supported to 2028; Node 26's first LTS is a week away and untested with our stack; Vite 8.3.5 is a day old, so pin it by lockfile.

principles.principle: Pin a WebGL2 stack now, plan WebGPU later. R3F v10 alpha is WebGPU-first, postprocessing (three <0.187) and N8AO are WebGL-only and SunLight is WebGPU-only, but three r186 WebGPURenderer can fall back to a WebGL2 backend.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Lock three 0.186.x, R3F 9.8.x, drei 10.7.x, react 19.3.x, n8ao 2.0.1 in a committed lockfile. Use stock materials and keep post effects and shader patches (CSM, SoftShadows) behind one renderer adapter. Set shadows=percentage, never true. Schedule a WebGPURenderer and TSL spike after 10 Dec.

principles.principle: Render only when something changes, and measure frame time only while frames are drawn. drei PerformanceMonitor takes timestamps from useFrame, so idle gaps under frameloop=demand count as elapsed time and read as low fps (source read). R3F documents regress() for interaction-time drops, and drei AdaptiveDpr reads it. Anatomy's WebGL rules cap DPR near 1.5 and stop idle loops.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: frameloop=demand. At startup run a 2-3 s calibration with frameloop=always (our own sampler that ignores gaps over about 100 ms, or PerformanceMonitor mounted only then) and store the tier per device in localStorage as a convenience, with a visible manual toggle. During orbit and drag use performance.regress plus AdaptiveDpr; verify that dpr changes redraw (call invalidate()). Mount PerformanceMonitor only for tours. AO and soft-shadow accumulation only at rest. Node thumbnails: render once offscreen and cache as images, because View calls gl.render directly and skips composer effects. Handle webglcontextlost and restored.

principles.principle: Keep lines thin, calm and computed once. Anatomy's craft rules give the subject the boldest tone; EdgesGeometry lines suit permanent linework (a forum thread with 5 replies, one voice); drei Edges builds them on the main thread per mesh; Manifold keeps edges between different faceIDs and tracks originalID. Screen pixel widths are not print weights.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Viewport lines 1 to 1.5 px, silhouette darker than internal edges, context lighter. Compute feature edges in the kernel worker (originalID boundaries plus a dihedral threshold for twisted or tapered faces, to be tested) and send one merged LineSegments2 per layer. drei Edges only for small imports. Outlines for hover, postprocessing Outline for multi-select; no full-scene edge detection by default. Print weights are set in mm in the vector path (see the board principle).

principles.principle: Monochrome with one lit accent, and every colour a token with light and dark values. Anatomy and Hairline both reserve colour for the subject; Hairline exposes plate, hi, edge, mid, lo and stroke-width tokens. Agent-generated hero art is slow and token-hungry (Anatomy's documented example took about 1 h 54 min; two runs differ), so time-box it.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Clay-and-hairline palette plus one accent for selection and hover. Token ladder plate/hi/edge/mid/lo/accent mapped to viewport and UI, plate equal to viewport background, separate dark values. Reserve the FALSE ASSUMPTION colour and analysis false-colour ramps so no UI chrome uses them (our inference). At most a few hero figures from anatomy or hairline-create, each with a spend cap, cached in the repo and never regenerated per user; routine UI art uses Hairline's static package.

principles.principle: Interaction respects attention and access. Anatomy motion.md: parts follow targets with springs or exponential easing, the loop sleeps when idle or offscreen, reduced motion jumps to end state, the selected assembly is the single lit accent. A forum thread (4 voices, none disputing) backs a semantic DOM mirror, keyboard use and live regions; @react-three/a11y is stale.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Apply to explode sliders, camera bookmarks and node hover; cap frame dt at 1/30 s. Hit areas that stay still, short tweens for discrete picks, a designed rest pose and clamped reach appear in neither Hairline nor Anatomy: record as team assumptions. Mirror node list and metrics in a hidden HTML layer with live regions; full keyboard navigation; no autoplay beyond user-started tours.

principles.principle: Section cuts are a stencil-plus-clipping recipe; plan, section and axon drawing geometry should come from the mesh kernel and three-edge-projection, not the render pass. In r186 an override material replaces the mesh material in a pass, so per-material clipping planes do not carry over, while renderer-level planes are global (source read).
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Viewport sections: clipping planes plus stencil caps on watertight meshes; test EffectComposer stencilBuffer, N8AO and Outline together, and fall back to renderer-level clippingPlanes if Outline leaks. Board drawings: Manifold slice() polygons to SVG for poche and floor plans; three-edge-projection for hidden-line roof, plan and (pre-rotated, untested) axon views, and PlanarIntersectionGenerator or slice for section lines.

principles.principle: For towers, mesh kernels beat B-rep kernels: massing needs extrude, twist, taper, booleans, area and volume. B-rep WASM is large (replicad build about 23 MB, opencascade.js about 9 MB, occt-wasm about 4.5 MB brotli) and mainly serves detail parts.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Massing nodes run on Manifold in a worker and report volume, gross floorplate area per floor (slice at mid-storey, since slice at the bottom returns the base faces and at the top returns empty) and surface area. FSR exclusions belong to the policy module. Offer replicad or occt-wasm only as optional v1 detail modules loaded on demand.

principles.principle: Heavy kernels and parsers belong in web workers, with manual memory management and cancellable work. Rhino3dmLoader decodes in workers; occt-wasm provides OcctWorker and requires release(); Manifold objects need explicit delete(). Manifold's ExecutionContext reports progress and cancels, but deferred operations (booleans, transforms) ignore it until an eager call such as status().
principles.rule_for_our_tool: One kernel worker pool with a typed message API. Each node result carries a dispose hook. Wire the progress and cancel UI to ExecutionContext (withContext) and call status() after each boolean chain; for slider drags debounce and terminate the worker instead of relying on long cancels. Delete contexts explicitly.

principles.principle: AI geometry generation is unreliable for free-form CAD and is trained on mechanical parts. Reported figures: 69.3% exact match for a fine-tuned model on single parts, +5% from visual feedback, no Zoo benchmarks. Text2BIM uses a rule-checker repair loop. A Hacker News thread (about 10 voices) says LLMs are weak at spatial reasoning. Structured-output limits differ: Claude rejects recursion, numeric bounds and array bounds beyond minItems 0 or 1, and caps optional parameters at 24 and anyOf or type-array parameters at 16; OpenAI strict mode allows recursion and bounds, up to 10 nesting levels and 5,000 properties.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Text-to-massing: the LLM returns a flat JSON node list (enum node types, id references, params as name/value pairs, all fields required) that passes both providers' schema rules; test the one schema against both APIs. Our validator checks positive volume, manifoldness, bounds and graph acyclicity with Manifold, then we render and let the user edit. Log every AI output as an editable team assumption.

principles.principle: Licence hygiene decides what ships. AGPL (xeokit, Theatre Studio) and LGPL WASM (OCCT builds) carry obligations; MPL-2.0 (web-ifc, ifc-lite) is file-level; Zlib, MIT, Apache-2.0 and CC0 are easy. N8AO is CC0 on GitHub but ISC on npm. Third-party tile services add terms (Google Map Tiles policy).
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Decide the platform's own licence first (open question for the team). Keep a THIRD_PARTY licence table in the repo; ship LGPL WASM with source and relink notice; never bundle AGPL code unless the platform is AGPL; record service terms for any streamed tiles before they reach a board.

principles.principle: Prefer in-browser WASM over native Python on student Windows machines, and fix the runtime once. Smart App Control can block unsigned OCP, CadQuery pip supports Python 3.9-3.12, and Node is not yet installed. Node 24 entered Maintenance on 2026-10-20 (supported to 2028-04-30); 22 ends 2027-04-30; 26 becomes LTS on 2026-10-28; Vite 8.3.5 needs Node ^20.19 or >=22.12.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Core runs in the browser with no native installs beyond Node 24.22.x, pinned in .nvmrc and package.json engines (do not start on 22). Any Python CAD stays optional: OCP.wasm in the browser or a documented WSL/conda path, with telemetry opt-out.

principles.principle: One canonical project frame, converted at the boundaries. Manifold slices on the X-Y plane (Z-up) and its JS Mesh is Float32; Rhino and IFC are Z-up; glTF is +Y up in metres; OBJ has no unit field; SketchUp exports Z-up with a units option; the official three.js 3dm example sets DEFAULT_UP to Z. Vancouver LiDAR 2022 is UTM 10 NAD83(CSRS), CGVD28GVRD, near 491,200 E and 5,458,900 N downtown (our calculation); float32 steps 0.5 m at that northing.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Project file stores metres, Z-up, site origin (block centroid), CRS (EPSG:3157 or 26910, confirmed per dataset) and vertical datum. Importers convert in float64 (proj4js) to local metres: Rhino modelUnitSystem, modelBasePoint and earthAnchorPoint; IFC unit scaling, GetCoordinationMatrix and IfcMapConversion with its Scale (Revit exports it only in IFC4; verify); glTF as metres Y-up; OBJ asks for units; portal GeoJSON is EPSG:4326. One root transform maps to three's Y-up (or DEFAULT_UP Z, decided in the spike). Tests: a 10 m cube in mm .3dm, m .ifc and OBJ gives 1000 m3 and 100 m2 per slice; two IFCs from one Revit model with shared coordinates overlay within 1 mm; a context tile round-trips within 1 mm.

principles.principle: Size the world from the sun, not from the model. At 49.28 N on 21 Dec the noon sun is about 17.3 degrees (our calculation: geometric, solar time, flat terrain): a 305 m tower casts about 980 m at noon, 1.4 km at 10:00 and 2.5 km at 09:00; equinox noon about 355 m. A few-hundred-metre default cuts shadows short, and a 2 km site stretches the depth range. reversedDepthBuffer is init-time and needs EXT_clip_control.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: The analysis window (dates, hours) is an editable team assumption (the policy packet may fix it). Domain = height / tan(lowest altitude in window) plus margin: about 1.5 km north for 10:00-14:00 on 21 Dec, about 2.5 km for 09:00-15:00. Set context data scope, shadow-camera fit (and CSM maxFar if used), BVH extent and analysis grid from it; coarse LOD far out. Fit near/far per frame; spike reversedDepthBuffer with N8AO and caps; avoid logarithmic depth unless N8AO is confirmed with it.

principles.principle: Boards need a capture pipeline, not a screenshot. A2 at 300 dpi is 4961 x 7016 px (34.8 Mpx; about 139 MB per RGBA8 buffer, our arithmetic). setViewOffset renders sub-rectangles of a larger frustum, but N8AO, SMAA and Outline sample neighbouring pixels, so tiles seam unless padded (SMAA presets search 4 to 32 px). At 300 dpi one pixel is 0.085 mm, so 1-1.5 px lines print near 0.1 mm.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Render tiles with a gutter (start 128 px, covering SMAA ULTRA and the AO radius), then crop; keep N8AO radius in world units. No raster linework in print captures: all lines come from the vector path (Manifold slices, three-edge-projection) with weights in mm, starting from the ISO 128 series (0.13, 0.18, 0.35, 0.5 mm; secondary sources; team assumption). Seam test: 2x2 tiled vs single render at a GPU-allowed size. Export clean depth, normal and line passes for gpt-image. Query GL limits at runtime; test on the weakest laptop before 13 Nov. Layout stays with the presentation packet.

principles.principle: Keep the massing graph deterministic, tagged and cheap to re-run. Manifold carries originalID and runIndex through booleans so program tags follow geometry; the node canvas (xyflow, MIT, 38.7k stars) and the 3D viewport should read one store so a parameter change recomputes only affected nodes.
principles.rule_for_our_tool: Reserve IDs per program volume and map them back to materials and GFA by program. Cache kernel results by hash of parameters plus upstream hashes; undo and redo then replay cached nodes (our design inference, to be tested). Test: podium union tower minus site cut keeps retail, office and residential tags.

recommendations.decision: Adopt Vite 8.3 + React 19.3 + TypeScript + three 0.186.1 + R3F 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 on the WebGL2 renderer, pinned in a committed lockfile (npm, npm ci), with Canvas shadows=percentage. Install Node 24.22.x now and pin it in .nvmrc and engines; lock n8ao 2.0.1. Keep COMPAT and THIRD_PARTY files (three below 0.187, react below 19.4, monthly upgrade check, licence table, AGPL blocked in CI, LGPL WASM shipped with source notice). Accept npm's auto-install of manifold-3d's peers (esbuild-wasm, gltf-transform) and confirm in the Vite bundle report that only manifold.js and the wasm ship; add npm overrides for three-edge-projection's stale peers.
recommendations.rationale: Peer ranges line up today (R3F react >=19 <19.4, postprocessing three <0.187, That Open three >=0.182) and Vite 8.3.5 needs Node ^20.19 or >=22.12. Node 24 entered Maintenance on 2026-10-20 but is supported to 2028-04-30, while 22 ends 2027-04-30. R3F 9.8.2's default soft shadows hit a mode r186 removed. A small compat file prevents rework before 13 Nov.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: R3F v10 alpha/WebGPU-first (pre-release, N8AO and postprocessing are WebGL-only); Babylon.js (ecosystem mismatch); raw three.js without R3F; floating caret versions; Node 22; waiting for Node 26 LTS (28 Oct) before starting; a pnpm packageExtensions workaround (not tested).

recommendations.decision: Default look 'Clay and Hairline': matte white massing, 1 to 1.5 px screen linework from kernel-computed feature edges, the built-in <N8AO halfRes /> from @react-three/postprocessing with multisampling 0, SMAA, tone mapping, Outlines for hover, one accent. Presets: Section (ortho plus stencil caps, tested with Outline on clipped meshes), Exploded axon, Analysis (false colour), Diagram (halftone/Kuwahara). Node-card thumbnails are rendered once offscreen and cached as images.
recommendations.rationale: Matches the instructor-shared tools' restraint and uses cheap existing components. Kernel edges avoid per-mesh main-thread EdgesGeometry hitches. drei View calls gl.render directly (source read), so live Views would miss composer effects and need continuous frames under xyflow pan and zoom; cached images avoid both.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Photoreal PBR as default (heavy on laptops, distracts from analysis); full-scene screen-space edge detection (extra pass, noisy); a custom N8AO wrapper; drei Edges for massing and context; live drei Views for every node card.

recommendations.decision: Use Manifold (manifold-3d 3.5.4) in a worker as the massing and boolean kernel in Z-up metres: extrude (twist/taper), union/subtract, slice-to-area at mid-storey, volume, project and section split. Carry program tags with reserveIDs/originalID, compute feature edges in the worker and send merged line segments, cache results by parameter hash, and drive progress and cancel through ExecutionContext plus status().
recommendations.rationale: One 2.8 MB-unpacked package covers tower massing, per-floor gross area and sections; guaranteed-manifold booleans reduce debugging; tags and edges come from the same mesh output. slice() at the bottom returns base faces and at the top returns empty, so slice mid-storey and label the result 'gross floorplate area'. Replicad or occt-wasm only as optional v1 detail modules.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: opencascade.js (stale since 2023); JSCAD (BSP booleans, anecdotal speed and manifoldness problems); three-bvh-csg (experimental, needs manifold inputs); CadQuery or build123d via Pyodide in core (not in the official package list; OCP.wasm roadmap only).

recommendations.decision: Add a canonical-frame rule to the project file and every importer: metres, Z-up kernel and analysis frame, site origin at the block centroid, CRS (EPSG:3157 or 26910, confirmed per dataset), offset and vertical datum stored; float64 transforms (proj4js) at import and export; Manifold, BVH and three.js receive local coordinates only; one root transform maps to the Y-up render frame (or DEFAULT_UP Z, chosen in the spike). Unit tests: a 10 m cube in mm .3dm, m .ifc and OBJ gives 1000 m3 and 100 m2 per slice; two IFCs from one Revit model with shared coordinates overlay within 1 mm; a context tile round-trips within 1 mm.
recommendations.rationale: Mixed units and axes fail silently: mm read as metres is a 1e6 area error and a Z/Y mix-up slices the tower sideways. Vancouver LiDAR is UTM 10 near 5.46 million m northing, where float32 steps 0.5 m. Manifold's JS Mesh is Float32, so the fix precedes the kernel. Rhino, IFC and Manifold are Z-up, glTF is Y-up in metres, OBJ has no unit field, and web-ifc offers a coordination matrix, a scaling factor and IfcMapConversion entities.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Rendering in raw UTM coordinates; relying on float64 inside the Manifold kernel (JS API is Float32); xeokit double-precision viewer (AGPL, separate renderer); letting each importer pick its own frame; web-ifc COORDINATE_TO_ORIGIN per file (misaligns multi-file projects).

recommendations.decision: Importers and context for 13 Nov: .3dm via Rhino3dmLoader with local rhino3dm wasm, IFC read via web-ifc 0.0.78 in a worker, OBJ/glTF via three loaders; export glTF (GLTFExporter) and .3dm. Analysis context comes from City LiDAR 2022 (buildings class), pre-processed offline into a compact glTF for the analysis domain; footprints 2015 for comparison only. v1: 3d-tiles-renderer for optional visual context after a Google and Cesium terms check, behind the importer interface; spikes: web-ifc vs ifc-lite vs IfcOpenShell on a real Revit IFC (load, fidelity, IFC4X3, write-back), and That Open Fragments in the R3F scene vs a lazy BIM inspector.
recommendations.rationale: All run client-side with no server cost. LiDAR tiles are 16 MB to 2.74 GB zipped, too large for the browser; footprints are 2015, approximate, without heights. Google tiles bar offline use, analysis and tracing 3D objects, so they suit live visuals only. IFC write-back with web-ifc is a low-level entity API, so it moves to v1.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: xeokit (AGPL-3.0); Speckle viewer as the viewport (Viewer 2 cannot render current bundles); Google tiles as analysis geometry (terms); loading raw LAS in the browser; promising IFC export for 13 Nov; mixing That Open's renderer beside R3F untested.

recommendations.decision: Implement text-to-massing, not free-form text-to-CAD: the LLM returns a flat JSON node list (enum node types, id references, params as name/value pairs, no recursion, no numeric bounds) through structured outputs; Manifold validates (volume, manifoldness, bounds, acyclic graph), we render and check, and the user edits parameters. Follow Text2BIM's checker-and-repair pattern. Install earthtojake/text-to-cad only as a developer Claude Code plugin for small details; Zoo API only as an optional flagged integration later.
recommendations.rationale: Published text-to-CAD results come from single mechanical parts (69.3% exact match at best); Text2BIM is the architecture-specific precedent. Claude structured outputs reject recursive schemas, numeric and most array bounds and cap optional parameters at 24, so a nested graph schema returns 400 errors; OpenAI strict mode is looser, so one flat schema serves both and our validator owns bounds.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Free-form LLM-to-CadQuery in core; Zoo Text-to-CAD as a dependency (hosted engine, credit cost, no benchmarks); cad0 (7B-class mechanical-part model); nested or recursive graph schemas.

recommendations.decision: Sun and shadow: SunCalc 2.1.1 behind one tested wrapper drives a directional light in WebGL with shadows=percentage; drei Sky for the sky; accumulate soft ground shadows only when still. Size the analysis domain from the sun window (about 1.5 km north for 10:00-14:00 on 21 Dec, 2.5 km for 09:00-15:00; team assumption). One-day spike on three 0.186.1: a single light with its shadow camera fitted to the domain (4096 map) vs CSM vs AccumulativeShadows; use CSM only if near-camera texels look poor; drop SoftShadows from core. Compute shadow hours analytically by BVH raycasts from grid points, not rendered pixels.
recommendations.rationale: Analysis must be reproducible and citable while the visual shadow is only illustrative. Our calculation gives a 305 m tower a noon shadow of 980 m on 21 Dec, so a few-hundred-metre default silently truncates it. CSM patches shaders and will not port to WebGPU; SunLight is WebGPU-documented; PCFSoftShadowMap was removed in r186; takram is beta.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: SunLight addon now (WebGPU only); takram atmosphere now; CSM by default; SoftShadows in core; AccumulativeShadows as the analysis source (planar ground catcher); default shadows=true.

recommendations.decision: Board capture service (owner needed): render the raster underlay (clay, AO, shadows) in tiles with camera.setViewOffset and a gutter of at least 128 px (SMAA ULTRA searches 32 px; AO radius in world units), then crop and stitch on the CPU. Print linework comes only from the vector path (Manifold slices, three-edge-projection) with weights in mm (0.13/0.18/0.35/0.5, a team assumption from the ISO 128 series), via svg2pdf.js and jsPDF (both MIT). Export clean depth, normal and line passes for gpt-image. Pass a 2x2 tiled vs single-render seam test and test on the weakest laptop before 13 Nov.
recommendations.rationale: Four A2 boards at 300 dpi need 4961 x 7016 px each; one canvas at that size plus AO, SMAA and outline buffers can exceed integrated-GPU memory. Screen-space passes lack data beyond a tile edge, so seams appear without padding, and pixel widths of 1-1.5 px print at about 0.1 mm.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Single full-size canvas capture; screenshots of the live viewport; raster linework in print; ungutted tiles; pdf-lib (last release 2021).

recommendations.decision: Performance budget and measured spikes: frameloop demand; startup tier calibration with frameloop=always (own sampler or PerformanceMonitor mounted only then); interaction-time DPR via performance.regress plus AdaptiveDpr; instancing, BVH picking, N8AO half-res, cached thumbnails, Low/Medium/High tiers with a visible toggle, context-loss handling. Before 13 Nov run and log measured numbers for: S1 shadows (fitted light vs CSM), S2 section (stencil + composer + N8AO + Outline), S3 depth (near/far fit vs reversedDepthBuffer on a 2 km scene), S4 twisted-tower edges (worker vs drei Edges), S5 tile seams, S6 unit and frame tests, S7 weakest-laptop smoke test; S8 real Revit IFC importer comparison by 10 Dec.
recommendations.rationale: PerformanceMonitor counts idle gaps as slow frames under frameloop=demand (source read), so the two rules conflicted. Vendor figures (N8AO 2x-4x, BVH 500 rays at 60 fps, ifc-lite 5x) are unverified and nothing was measured on a team laptop, so each spike needs a pass/fail number. 23 days remain to 13 Nov, so S1-S7 fit about 5 working days.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: PerformanceMonitor permanently mounted under a demand loop; fixed high quality for everyone; many Canvas elements or live Views for node cards; WebGPU path-tracing for the live view (three-gpu-pathtracer needs WebGPU and long convergence).

recommendations.decision: Aesthetic system and resource handling: adopt Hairline's token ladder and @lucasmarkes/hairline for module cards, empty states and onboarding; take motion and WebGL rules from Anatomy's reference files; generate at most a few cached hero figures with a spend cap. Treat hairline, anatomy and text-to-cad as dev-time and design resources, not runtime dependencies, and verify with Xun which repositories she meant.
recommendations.rationale: Gives a consistent calm visual language cheaply; hero art is expensive (about 2 h agent time per Anatomy example). These are third-party MIT repos, very new (Anatomy created 2026-10-08) and fast-changing; none sits in the xunliuDesign account. Interaction rules are re-sourced to their actual files.
recommendations.alternatives_rejected: Per-module generated illustrations (token cost, inconsistent output); Theatre.js for motion (stalled, AGPL studio); animated attention-grabbing UI; vendoring their code; citing kaushikhegde11/hairline-anatomy (0 stars) for interaction rules.
